grandĭfer , ĕra, ĕrum, adj. grandisfero,
I.bearing or producing great things, productive: “hae arationes,” Cic. Phil. 2, 39, 101 ; cf. Mart. Cap. 5, § 511: “loci facies palmis arboribus grandifera, Auct. Itin. Alex. 20, 51: facta,” Nazar. Paneg. Const. 3 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
